title: Introduce RAG Telemetry Surgeon: compact debug & probe kit for replayable traces
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added a compact RAG debugging kit that provides token-level traces, deterministic replay harness, and telemetry sanitizers for local dev and CI smoke tests.
description:
Motivation: debugging downstream regressions caused by retrieval or KV-cache inconsistencies has been time-consuming—engineers need a tiny, reproducible toolset that captures token-level traces, attachment of retrieval snapshots, and a deterministic replay harness that runs headless in CI. This PR introduces the 'RAG Telemetry Surgeon' quickstart: a compact local kit with probes, sanitizers, and replay tooling for developers and SREs.

What this PR adds (single continuous description): Adds a new quickstart under quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon with: 1) a lightweight token-tracing shim that wraps Redwood client calls and emits per-step traces (prompt chunks, model selection, returned tokens, token timestamps), 2) a retrieval snapshot formatter that saves a normalized view of index hits and metadata for deterministic replays, 3) a replay harness (node script + Dockerfile) that can replay an entire RAG session end-to-end using recorded traces and optional mock index responses, 4) a telemetry sanitizer utility to redact PII and rotate request IDs for safe upload during triage, 5) example devcontainer and a CI job (GitHub Actions) used for smoke replays in PRs.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart folder and README with step-by-step local instructions - [x] Implement trace wrapper (JS) and CI replay workflow - [x] Add sanitization tool and tests - [x] Document how to hook into Redwood Console traces + sample dashboard queries - [x] Add license/NOTICE entry for helper libraries

Commits summary: - 3be2a9a add initial scaffolding and README - f9d7c4b implement token-trace wrapper and serializers - a7c4d12 add retrieval snapshot formatter and sample fixture - 5f11e30 add replay harness + dockerfile - b2a9e01 add sanitizer and unit tests - c9f88a0 update docs and CI workflow

Changed areas (high level): quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/README.md, quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/trace-wrapper/index.js, quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/replay/harness.js, quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/replay/Dockerfile, quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/sanitize/sanitizer.py, quickstarts/rag-telemetry-surgeon/fixtures/sample_trace.json, .github/workflows/rag-replay-smoke.yml, docs/observability/telemetry-surgeon.md, package.json

Review conversation summary: Priya: "Nice ergonomics. Two asks: add an option to output compressed traces and ensure the sanitizer flags are consistent across platforms." Maya: "Added compressed output flag (--compress) and normalized sanitizer flags in sanitizer.py; updated README with examples." Diego: "Can the replay harness run against a live dev index? We should limit default to mock mode to avoid accidental production hits." Maya: "Replay defaults to mock index; CLI accepts --live-index with explicit warning and requires REDWOOD_DEV=true. Documented in README." Jordan: "CI job looks good but add longer timeouts for cold-start tests (first-run latency)." Maya: "Increased action timeout to 20m and added retry for ephemeral failures." 

CI and checks: GitHub Actions matrix (node 18/20) run - lint: pass, unit tests: pass, integration/replay-smoke: pass on mock fixtures, packaging: pass. One flaky run initially in integration (timeout) — rerun passed.

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers (Priya, Diego). Merged via squash-and-merge. Notes: target quickstart intended for developer onboarding and SRE triage; not enabled by default in hosted examples but linked from docs/observability.
